gemini.rationale: The transaction bifurcated NewStar at closing: the customer-facing loan portfolio (T4) was sold to a GSO-sponsored entity, while the asset-management platform and capabilities (T5) were acquired by First Eagle, creating a clear structural mismatch between the product and its originating processes (gap_45 = 1). The operating workforce and processes moved together to First Eagle without a documented mismatch (gap_56 = 0).

grok.rationale: gap_45=1 because at closing the customer-facing loan and credit investment portfolio was carved out and sold to GSO Diamond Portfolio Holdco LLC while the asset-management platform, investment-management capability, and operating processes remained with the NewStar entity that passed to First Eagle, a documented product-vs-process ownership split (Structural summary; Product/asset carve-out; Form 8-K Item 2.01). gap_56=0 because the same closing structure transferred the platform/operations together with Continuing Employees under merger-agreement employee-matters provisions assuring salary, benefits, and service continuity, so T5 and T6 were aligned into First Eagle rather than separated; no TSA is documented as absorbing the T4/T5 gap with GSO (Employee Matters; Structural summary).

openai.rationale: The product/asset layer was structurally separated: NewStar's loan and credit-investment portfolio was sold to GSO immediately before the merger, while the asset-management platform and investment-management capability entered First Eagle's ownership, documenting a product-versus-process gap at closing. The operating capability transferred alongside the surviving company and its Continuing Employees, whose employment continuity and benefits were addressed in the merger agreement, so no process-versus-organization gap is documented. The slice expressly states that workforce continuity was not handled through a separate transitional-services arrangement, so the documented gap was not contractually mitigated through such an agreement.
